overall: The commission violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing topics at its July 8 meeting that were missing from the notice; its delayed approval of May 27 minutes was not a violation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the commission discussed topics at its July 8 meeting that were not listed on the notice posted at least 48 hours before the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because she knew at the time of posting this notice that she planned to discuss these specific items of correspondence at issue, she should have included those items on the July 8 notice.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the commission failed to approve its May 27 meeting minutes in a timely manner, with approval not coming until September 23.
allegations.key_passage: Here, although the minutes were not approved at the Commission's next meeting, the Commission made good faith- albeit unsuccessful- efforts to timely approve the minutes.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We therefore order the Commission's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that future similar conduct may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
